Ardmore Chamber of Commerce

What These Initiatives Will Accomplish

Outcomes straight from Ardmore’s
Economic Vision Plan.

The 2025 plan the Chamber co-commissioned says the marketing challenge is “not due to a lack of planning, but because of execution constraints.” These five initiatives are the execution.

Top of mind, out of market
Site selectors and entrepreneurs evaluate communities online — anonymously, long before they make contact. The audience we’ve built keeps Ardmore in that conversation.
A clear sense of place
The plan names the lack of “a clear sense of who Ardmore is” as a core weakness. A year of storytelling — and a rebuilt visitor site — is the answer.
Stronger small businesses
Diversifying beyond one large employer starts with the businesses already here. Training, visibility and measurable foot traffic, for all 587 members.
Talent that stays
The plan lists “loss of talent to larger cities” as a threat. Every open job in Ardmore, in one place, gives people a reason to stay — or come back.
Tourism assets, put to work
“Underutilized tourism assets” is the plan’s phrase. The discount card, the weekly round-up and a rebuilt Explore Ardmore put them in front of visitors.
Progress the board can report
The plan asks each organization to track and share its metrics annually. The measurement layer delivers the Chamber’s numbers — no added staff time.

2025 Economic Vision Plan — commissioned by the Ardmore Chamber of Commerce, Ardmore Development Authority and Ardmore Tourism Authority.
